extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent applicants and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive procedural requirements for preparing, filing, prosecuting, and appealing U.S. patent applications before the Patent Office and in court, including drawings, models, specimens, fees, examination, amendments, and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of final issue fee and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The final fee must be paid within six months after the patent is allowed; the patent must issue within three months after the fee is paid; if the fee is not paid within six months the statute provides that the patent shall be withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner of Patents has no jurisdiction to issue a patent when statute forbids (e.g., if final fee paid more than six months after allowance the patent would be void). At common law 'month' is a calendar month for patent statutes by judicial interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings required when invention admits representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are required by statute to be furnished by applicants in all cases wherein the invention admits of representation by drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory requirement is only that they be signed by applicant or attorney-in-fact, but Patent Office rules require drawings to show every feature of the invention covered by the claims. For improvements on old machines, drawings must exhibit the invention itself disconnected from the old structure and also another view showing so much of the old structure as will suffice to show the connection. Rules describe numerous other characteristics which must be carefully followed to secure favorable action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and purpose of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings should show the true positions and proportions of parts so far as necessary to show the invention; they need not be accurate enough to serve as working drawings for construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be as useful as possible, drawings should delineate positions and proportions necessary to show the invention; perfection to working-drawing tolerances is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference figures and labeling between drawings and specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Office rules require that drawings be connected to the specification by figures adjacent to views, and by letters or numerals adjacent to parts, and that those figures/letters/numerals be incorporated in the descriptive part of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier statutes required 'written references' on drawings; the present statute says nothing but the Office rules require the indicated coupling of drawing elements and specification text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models when invention admits model representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A model of the invention is required by statute to be furnished where the invention admits of representation by model, provided the Commissioner requires a model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision allows the Commissioner to dispense with models when their utility is inferior to their cost or space occupied; in practice models are called for in very few cases nowadays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens for compositions of matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens of compositions of matter and their ingredients are required to be furnished by applicants for such inventions in all cases where the Commissioner calls for such specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner usually calls for at least a specimen of the composition, put up to be preserved, unless the composition is perishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing date governs priority
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent dates from its filing in the Patent Office, not from execution by applicant, deposit of a model, or deposit of anything less than the full application; where an application is divided by filing a new one for part of its subject, the new one will date from the date of the old one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A memorandum on an issued patent stating the application filing date is not evidence of the fact unless admitted for the purpose without objection; proof of the application date must be supplemented by proof of the condition of the application at that date when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of patent attorneys/agents and who may represent applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: A register of attorneys is kept of all persons entitled to represent applicants before the Patent Office; no person whose name is not on that register may prosecute an application except on an invention he himself made or which has been assigned to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any attorney in good standing in a court of record may be admitted to the register upon furnishing a clerk's certificate. Non-attorneys may be admitted upon proof of good moral character and competence to render valuable services. Persons may be expelled for incompetence, disrepute, or gross misconduct, but only after notice and a hearing; Commissioner's disciplinary action must be approved by the Secretary of the Interior before enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: While an application is pending, the Commissioner has no authority to furnish a copy of any paper belonging to it to anyone except the applicant or his attorney/agent; no Patent Office official may give information about a pending application except as the Patent Office rules authorize limited information to those who make or represent an interfering application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Office officials should not take notice of statements relevant to patentability made by persons not in privity with the application; written statements by third parties may be returned as impertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's duty to examine and issue patents
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is made, it is the Commissioner's duty to cause an examination of the application and the invention; if the applicant is justly entitled under the law, it is the duty of the Commissioner to issue a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination may extend beyond novelty to any question on which patentability may depend; Patent Office officials may base judgments upon any books, publications or records they think proper; the Commissioner need not prescribe which subordinate conducts the examination and may overrule subordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment on rejection — notice and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, after examination, an application is rejected, the Commissioner must notify the applicant, giving the reasons for the rejection together with information and references useful in judging the propriety of prosecuting the application or altering the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after receiving such notice the applicant persists in his request for a patent, with or without altering the specification, it becomes the Commissioner's duty to cause a re-examination of the case. The rules for division and appeals (e.g., Rule 41) affect entitlement to further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal within the Patent Office (primary examiner → board → Commissioner)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, without amending the specification, the applicant persists and the primary examiner again rejects, the applicant may appeal to the board of examiners-in-chief; if unsuccessful there he may appeal to the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All appeals must be heard on the case as submitted to the primary examiner; no appeal should be taken until the application is in such condition that a reversal would permit issuance; if the board reverses the examiner the examiner must pass the case for issue; the Commissioner will not reverse the board on questions of fact unless its decision was clearly against the weight of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy when examiner refuses to forward appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Examiner refuses to forward an appeal and the Commissioner refuses to compel him, the remedy is to apply to the Court of Appeals of the District of Columbia for a writ of mandamus to compel transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal to the board may be heard by the Commissioner or an Assistant Commissioner under assignment; if an Assistant Commissioner hears it, no appeal lies from his decision to the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's power to reconsider Patent Office actions before issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may at any time before the issue of a patent reverse his own or any other favorable Patent Office action thereon, except that of a predecessor of himself or of a predecessor of the Assistant Commissioner, and may thereupon reject the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions of predecessors are protected except as to fraud, clerical error apparent on the face of the record, or newly discovered evidence presented under circumstances justifying a new trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the Court of Appeals of the District of Columbia — scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commissioner or Assistant Commissioner finally rejects an application, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Appeals of the District of Columbia; no appeal lies to the Secretary of the Interior. Appeals to that court are limited to final rejections of applications and final awards of priority in interference cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commissioner refuses to allow the appeal, mandamus may compel him to do so. The appellant must notify the Commissioner and file reasons for the appeal in the Patent Office within the time the Commissioner appoints. The court confines review to points set forth in the appellant's reasons and will not review Patent Office practice unless a substantial right was affected and there was an abuse of discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and evidence on appeal to the court
rubrics_metrics.description: On appeal the appellant must lay before the court certified copies of all papers in the case; the Commissioner must furnish the court a full written statement of the grounds of his decision; the Commissioner and the examiners may be examined under oath if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers going from the applicant or Commissioner to the court are not kept secret in the court, though the original Patent Office papers remain concealed until final disposition. The court hears the case on the papers before the Commissioner and confines revision to the appellant's stated points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable bill in U.S. courts when patent/reissue refused
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a patent or reissue is refused by the Commissioner or by the Court of Appeals, the applicant may file a bill in equity in any U.S. court having or acquiring jurisdiction of the parties to seek a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complainant should be the inventor-applicant or assignee; the Secretary of the Interior is not a proper party. A District Court acquires jurisdiction of the Commissioner only by his voluntary appearance; the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia has jurisdiction by virtue of the Commissioner's official residence. The court may adjudge the applicant entitled to receive a patent for the invention as specified in his final claims (not for claims relinquished or never presented), and such adjudication authorizes the Commissioner to issue the patent upon filing a copy and complying with law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard and scope in equity suits to procure patent
rubrics_metrics.description: In an equity bill to procure a patent the court will take testimony and admissible evidence according to equity practice and will consider what was before the Patent Office and (if applicable) the Court of Appeals; testimony taken in an interference proceeding is generally incompetent except as permitted by secondary evidence rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The burden is on the complainant to prove the truth of his bill by clear and conclusive evidence even if the defendant defaults. Such suits are original and not merely reviews of Patent Office proceedings; appeals to the Court of Appeals must be exhausted where available before resorting to the bill in equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for equitable suit
rubrics_metrics.description: The remedy by bill in equity must be invoked within one year after the last official action on the application, unless the complainant satisfies the court that the longer delay was unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisition pending suit of an issued patent in interference by the adverse party does not abate the suit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to amend specifications and statutory notice on rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to amend applications is of great value; although not expressly established by statute originally, statutes (since 1870 and continuing) require that whenever any claim is rejected the Commissioner should notify the applicant and furnish information useful in judging the propriety of altering his specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The present statute on the subject is substantially identical with the 1870 provision: rejection triggers notice and information to assist the applicant in considering amendment.
